title: sweep() has no access control: anyone can send the vault's entire native balance to any address
description: Discovery: Q3.7 / MODIFIER-01. sweep() is external with no guards (facts.json entry_points guards = []), while setFee and transferOwnership use onlyOwner. It transfers address(this).balance to a caller-chosen address. The in-code comment marks it a planted bug, so it is not intentional design; known-issues.md lists nothing.
root_cause: A value-moving function lacks any caller check and ignores the per-user balances ledger that depositEth maintains.

harm.magnitude: 100% of the vault's native balance in one call

exploit_trace: 1. Victims call depositEth() and the vault holds N wei.
2. Attacker calls sweep(attacker) from any EOA.
3. to.transfer(address(this).balance) sends N wei to the attacker.
4. Victims' balances[] entries still show N wei credited but nothing backs them.

preconditions.text: the vault holds a non-zero native balance

audit_trail.step_execution: Gates: A=✓ B=✓ C=✓ D=✓ E=✓ F=✓ G=✓ H=✓

verdict.reason: Survived gates A-H; src/Vault.sol:32-34 has no caller check, recon/known-issues list nothing. Strong consensus. PoC recommended (Critical).

title: ETH and token deposits share one balances ledger: an ETH depositor can withdraw other users' tokens
description: Discovery: Q3.2 (paired operation symmetry) and BL-03 (dual accounting). depositEth() credits balances[msg.sender] by msg.value, and withdraw() debits the same mapping but pays out `token`. The two assets are different, with no conversion or price relation, so wei credited by ETH can be redeemed one-for-one as token units.
root_cause: A single balances mapping tracks two unrelated assets, and withdraw() only pays the ERC20.

harm.magnitude: up to the vault's whole token balance, for a cost of the same number of wei

exploit_trace: 1. Victims deposit 1,000,000 token units via deposit().
2. Attacker calls depositEth{value: 1_000_000 wei}(), crediting balances[attacker] = 1,000,000.
3. Attacker calls withdraw(1_000_000): the balances debit passes, and token.transfer sends 1,000,000 token units to the attacker.
4. The attacker's 1,000,000 wei stays in the vault, so the victims' tokens are gone and the attacker can recover the wei through sweep().

preconditions.text: the vault holds tokens deposited by others

postconditions.text: token holdings fall below the sum of token depositors' balances; totalDeposits wraps (see DP1-4)

audit_trail.step_execution: Gates: A=✓ B=✓ C=✓ D=✓ E=✓ F=✓ G=✓ H=✓
rules_applied: R10:✓(assessed at the fully funded vault)
postconditions_created: token holdings below sum of token depositors' balances

verdict.reason: Survived gates A-H; depositEth (l.28) credits balances, withdraw (l.37,41) debits it and pays token with no asset separation; reachable by anyone. Trace confirmed with values. PoC recommended.

title: No way to withdraw ETH: ETH deposits are only recoverable as tokens or taken by sweep()
description: Discovery: Module W / MISSING-02 (exit-path coverage). The only native-value exit is sweep(), which ignores balances[]. withdraw() pays only the ERC20. An ETH depositor therefore has no path to reclaim their ETH. If the vault holds no tokens, withdraw reverts at the transfer or pays nothing, and their credit is worthless.
root_cause: depositEth() credits a ledger entry, but no function pays ETH out against it.

harm.loses_what: their deposited ETH, permanently locked or stolen by the first sweep caller

exploit_trace: 1. Alice calls depositEth{value: 1 ether}() and balances[alice] = 1e18.
2. Alice calls withdraw(1e18). With no token balance in the vault, token.transfer cannot pay and the call reverts or pays nothing of value.
3. No other function sends ETH against balances[alice].
4. Any observer can call sweep() and take Alice's ETH.

preconditions.text: a user deposits ETH via depositEth

postconditions.text: ETH sits in the vault with no rightful redemption path

verdict.reason: Survived gates A-H; no function pays native currency against balances[] (only sweep, which ignores the ledger), so ETH credits are unredeemable and takeable via sweep. Distinct root cause from DP1-1 (missing exit path vs missing auth).

title: withdraw() subtracts totalDeposits in an unchecked block, so totalDeposits wraps to about 2^256 when it is out of sync with balances
description: Discovery: Q3.5 (overflow protection consistency). balances[msg.sender] -= amount is checked, but totalDeposits -= amount is in unchecked{}. depositEth() raises balances without raising totalDeposits, so a withdrawal funded by ETH credit makes totalDeposits underflow silently. The public totalDeposits value becomes garbage, and any integration or future logic that reads it is corrupted.
root_cause: The unchecked subtraction assumes totalDeposits >= every balance, which depositEth() breaks.

harm.who: integrators and users relying on totalDeposits
harm.loses_what: an accurate total-deposits figure; no direct in-contract fund loss
harm.magnitude: totalDeposits reads about 2^256 minus the withdrawn amount

exploit_trace: 2. Attacker calls withdraw(1): balances is checked and passes, then totalDeposits = 0 - 1 wraps to 2^256-1.

preconditions.text: balances[user] exceeds the share of totalDeposits backing it (ETH credit)

postconditions.text: totalDeposits permanently desynchronised from real deposits

audit_trail.step_execution: Gates: A=✓ B=✓ C=✓ D=✓ E=✓ F=✓ G=✓ H=✓

verdict.reason: Mechanism confirmed at src/Vault.sol:38-40 (unchecked subtraction wraps when withdrawn amount exceeds totalDeposits, enabled by depositEth not updating it). Low severity: no direct fund loss, totalDeposits not used elsewhere in-contract.

title: deposit() credits the requested amount without checking transferFrom's result or the amount actually received
description: Discovery: rescan class 2 (asymmetric operations) and class 4 (economic edges). deposit() ignores the bool returned by token.transferFrom and credits balances and totalDeposits by the full requested amount. For a token that returns false instead of reverting (insufficient balance or allowance), or that takes a transfer fee, the credit exceeds what the vault received. withdraw() then pays out the full credited amount from other depositors' tokens. This is a different root cause from the shared ETH and token ledger in DP1-2.
root_cause: The credit is based on the caller-supplied amount rather than on a verified or balance-delta receipt of tokens.

harm.loses_what: deposited tokens paid out against unbacked credit
harm.magnitude: up to the vault's whole token balance when the token returns false on failure

exploit_trace: 1. Honest users deposit 1,000 token units; the vault holds 1,000.
2. Attacker with zero token balance calls deposit(1000); the token's transferFrom returns false without reverting and the return value is ignored.
4. Attacker calls withdraw(1000); token.transfer sends 1,000 units of other users' tokens to the attacker.

preconditions.text: the immutable token returns false on failed transferFrom, or charges a transfer fee

postconditions.text: vault token holdings are below the sum of token credits
